plan.chapterName: Anton, Bivens, and Davis. Calculus, 10th Edition, Figure 5.2.17
plan.contextChunk: This figure is part of a worked example asking to find the volume of the solid generated when the region under y = x^2 over [0, 2] is rotated about the line y = -1. The figure contains two linked views. Left (2D): the xy-plane showing the region R bounded above by the parabola y = x^2 and below by the x-axis between x = 0 and x = 2; the axis of revolution y = -1 is drawn as a horizontal red line, with a rotation arrow indicating revolution about it, and a representative washer cross-section at position x is sketched in gray. Right (3D): the resulting solid of revolution shown in perspective, with a visible central hole (from the inner radius of 1) and the parabolic outer surface. The figure illustrates the washer method: at each x, the cross-section is a washer with outer radius x^2 + 1 and inner radius 1, giving area pi((x^2 + 1)^2 - 1^2) = pi(x^4 + 2x^2), and the volume is computed by integrating this expression from 0 to 2.

interactions.label: Generating curve and axis
interactions.teaches: The washer dimensions come from both the curve and the rotation axis: the outer radius is f(x) - c while the inner radius is the distance from y = 0 to y = c

interactions.label: Slice position x
interactions.teaches: Sweeping the slice shows that the washer area changes with x, so the volume is the integral of these varying cross-sectional areas

demo_steps.title: Middle washer
demo_steps.narration: At x = 1 with f(x) = x^2 and c = -1, the outer radius is 2 and the inner radius is 1. The washer area is pi(2^2 - 1^2) = 3pi.

demo_steps.title: Near the start
demo_steps.narration: Near x = 0 the curve is close to the x-axis, so the outer and inner radii are nearly equal. The washer is very thin and contributes little volume.

demo_steps.title: Right endpoint
demo_steps.narration: At x = 2, the outer radius is 2^2 + 1 = 5 while the inner radius stays 1. This produces the largest washer, with area pi(25 - 1) = 24pi.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Use a mixed layout matching the source: the left 2D graph occupies the left half, the 3D solid occupies the right half, and the red rotation axis is one continuous horizontal line through both. World coordinates: set the left graph origin at approximately (-4.0, 0, 0). In the graph, one mathematical unit equals about 0.85 world units horizontally and vertically; show x from about -0.25 to 2.35 and y from -2.0 to 4.6. The default curve is y = x^2 over 0 <= x <= 2, so the region top reaches y = 4 at x = 2. Fill R with pale blue #c9e8f5 at about 55 percent opacity; draw the curve in bright blue #20a6df with line width 3; draw axes and boundary in dark gray/black #222222. The rotation axis is y = c, default c = -1, drawn red #ff5b63 as a thin horizontal line extending from the left label area through the 3D solid. The representative washer on the left is centered at the selected x position and y = c; for the default at x = 1, outer radius R = f(1) - c = 2 and inner radius r = 0 - c = 1. Draw it as a translucent gray annulus/ellipse, about 0.22 world units thick in screen x direction, with a white inner hole. The right solid starts around global X = 1.6 and ends around global X = 4.4; map mathematical x in [0,2] to this length. Use radius scale about 0.55 world units per mathematical radius for the 3D solid so the default maximum outer radius at x = 2 is 5 * 0.55 = 2.75 world units and the inner cylindrical radius is 1 * 0.55 = 0.55. The solid axis is horizontal, matching the red line at y = -1. Generate the default outer surface by revolving y = x^2 around y = -1: outer radius R(x) = x^2 + 1; inner radius r = 1. Washer area is A(x) = pi((x^2 + 1)^2 - 1^2) = pi(x^4 + 2x^2), and the corresponding default volume is integral from 0 to 2 of A(x) dx = 176pi/15. The 3D surface should be translucent gray #b8bdc2 with pale blue highlights #cfeaf7 on the upper outer surface; end rims and inner cylinder should be light gray with darker gray edge outlines.
interactionPlan.notes: Parse the equation input live. The f(x) field redraws the blue curve, filled region, outer surface, and the selected washer outer radius. The axis field should parse as a constant expression for c; the intended washer formula assumes c <= 0 and f(x) >= 0 on [0,2], so show an inline warning if the edited values violate that simple geometry. Build the 3D solid as parametric meshes: outer surface points use X = xStart + xScale*x, Y = c + radiusScale*(f(x) - c)*cos(theta), Z = radiusScale*(f(x) - c)*sin(theta); inner surface uses radiusScale*(0 - c). Use enough subdivisions, about 80 along x and 64 around theta, for smooth reshaping. Keep the left graph and labels camera-facing so they remain readable while the right solid retains slight perspective depth. The xSlice slider updates the left washer, the highlighted 3D washer ring, the vertical guide line, and the numeric callout each frame.

authoredContext: Find the volume of the solid generated when the region under the curve y = x2 over the interval [0, 2] is rotated about the line y =−1. Solution. First sketch the region and the axis of revolution; then imagine revolving the region about the axis (Figure 5.2.17). At each x in the interval 0 ≤ x ≤ 2, the cross section of the solid perpendicular to the axis y =−1 is a washer with outer radius x2 + 1 and inner radius 1. Since the area of this washer is A(x) = π([x2 + 1] 2 − 12 ) = π(x4 + 2x2 ) it follows by (3) that the volume of the solid is V = ! 2 0 A(x) dx = ! 2 0 π x4 + 2x2_x000b_ dx = π 1 5 x5 + 2 3 x3 _x0010_2 0 = 176π 15

discrepancies: The default perspective view makes the red rotation axis and left graph appear slanted, whereas the source presents the axis as a straight horizontal line through the composition.
The generated figure adds labels on the 3D solid such as “surface from f(x)=x^2” and “axis y=-1” that are not present in the source figure.
The right-hand solid is darker and more opaque than the light gray translucent textbook rendering, making the inner cylinder and end face visually heavier.
The selected washer is highlighted in bright blue on the 3D solid, which is pedagogically useful but not shown in the original source.
evaluation.notes: The generated figure captures the washer-method geometry and labels well, but adds extra explanatory elements and uses a slightly skewed/darker 3D presentation compared with the source.

Lighten the opacity and color of the right-hand solid to better match the pale gray translucent textbook style.
Remove or hide the extra labels on the 3D solid by default if strict visual fidelity to the source is desired.
Make the 3D highlighted washer optional through the control panel rather than always visible.
